items.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
items.summary: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it.…

items.summary: Coding agents can generate runnable games from natural-language descriptions. However, a runnable game does not guarantee an excellent gameplay experience for players. How agents can improve these aspects of playfulness remains underexplored. In our work, we propose Play2Evolve, a recursive game development framework with three stages: Initialization, Refinement, and Evolution.…

items.summary: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback. Medical question answering and diagnosis prediction have reference answers, whereas clinical inquiry has no single correct response and is judged with rubrics.…

We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts.…

Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity.…

In this paper, we present a generalizable pipeline that directly recovers continuous, high-fidelity 3D surfaces from unposed images by seamlessly integrating pointmap- and ray-based representations. Specifically, Qwen3.5-0.8B reads its own weights, proposes an edit, and then continues with the edited weights as both problem solver and editor. We find many cases of genuine self-improvement.…

items.summary: Fixes #31680 The matmul_tiled() implementation in tinyBLAS_Q0_PPC requires nc to be a multiple of 8 to perform matrix multiplication correctly. The previous alignment logic contained a special case for n == 4, which allowed n_aligned to be 4. Consequently, the tiled path could be selected with nc = 4, violating the kernel's tile-width requirement. This caused incorrect matrix multiplication results, observed as garbled inference output when running Flint Q4_K_M and Gemma 3 27B Instruct.
